content:
Hi everyone,

Sharing an upcoming philosophy event I'm organising that should be of interest to some of you (with keynotes from Michael Harris, Kati Kish, Ursula Martin, and Emily Riehl!). Registration for in person attendance is open, but note that it will also be livestreamed. Details below.

All the best,
Fenner

Call for Registrations: Mathematical Proof in the Age of AI, Bergen, Norway, 7-8 October 2026

Dear all,

We are delighted to announce the full programme for the upcoming conference Mathematical Proof in the Age of AI, to be held in Bergen, Norway, 7-8 October 2026.

Full details of the event can be found here:

https://www4.uib.no/en/research/research-groups/philosophy-of-science-and-mathematics/events/mathematical-proof-in-the-age-of-ai-implications-of-the-use-of-artificial-intelligence-in-mathematical-research

Details on how to register for in-person attendance can be found on the website. Please register by the 5th October.

Additionally, the whole conference will be livestreamed, with details to follow on the website (no registration is required for this).

Organised by: Sorin Bangu, Ásgeir Berg Matthíasson, Fenner Stanley Tanswell

All the best,

Sorin, Ásgeir, and Fenner

Day 1: Wednesday 7th October

9:00-9:15 Welcome by Sorin, Ásgeir, and Fenner

9:15-10:30 KEYNOTE Ursula Martin (Oxford, Edinburgh) The Leiden Declaration on AI and mathematics: roots, reception and reflection.

11:00-11:45 Fenner Tanswell (TU Berlin) On Autoformalisation

11:45-12:30 Markus Pantsar (RWTH Achen) Trust in mathematical AI systems

12:30-14:00 Lunch

14:00-14:45 Carolin Antos (Konstanz) Notions of (AI)-proofs

14:45-15:30 Michael Friedman (Bonn) Anxiety and Opacity: From AI-generated Proofs to Autoformalization

16:00-16:45 David Appadourai (Rome) Bidirectionality and the Epistemic Limits of Machine-Verified Proof

17:00-18:15 KEYNOTE Kati Kish Bar On (Boston Univ. and Harvard Business School - AI Institute) Rethinking Mathematical Intuition, Agency, and Practice in the Age of AI

Day 2: Thursday 8th October

9:15-10:30 KEYNOTE Emily Riehl (Johns Hopkins, Baltimore) A new paradigm for mathematical proof?

11:00-11:45 Silvia De Toffoli (IUSS Pavia) After Math

11:45-12:30 Ásgeir Berg (Iceland) Mathematical Understanding in the Time of Astra

12:30-14:00 Lunch

14:00-14:45 José Pérez-Escobar (Madrid) LLMs and rule-following in mathematics

14:45-15:30 Romain Büchi (Geneva) Conjecturing with AI: A View from Mathematical Practice

16:00-16:45 Sorin Bangu (Bergen) Rule-following and Rule-breaking: How is Mathematical Creativity Possible (in the Age of AI)

17:00-18:15 KEYNOTE Michael Harris (Columbia, NYC) Purity as organizing principle
(I think the url markdown is misformed fyi)

Livestreamed and left up on YT for later viewing? A recent conference I was interested was livestreamed but was not in my timezone and not kept, rendering my registration moot. Sorry to have to ask...

This was a good question, in the sense that I did not know the answer. I have now checked, and leaving them online and available is the plan. (The one caveat is that we need the speakers' permission. While we have informed them all that this is indeed the idea, we still need them to sign the forms!)
Oh, that is of course appropriate, thanks for checking.
